summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 1 diabetes, poorly controlled with prior DKA admissions, alcohol use disorder in recovery, and depression presented with nausea, vomiting, and hyperglycemia. She was diagnosed with diabetic ketoacidosis likely triggered by a urinary tract infection. She was treated in the emergency department with IV fluids, an insulin drip, and ceftriaxone. After stabilization, she was admitted to the medicine service, transitioned back to her home insulin regimen, and completed a short course of oral antibiotics. Her condition improved rapidly, with resolution of DKA and stable vital signs. She was discharged home with instructions to continue insulin, complete antibiotics, and follow up with her primary care provider and specialists within one week.
